subjects.label: Villager species
subjects.description: The animal peoples who settle the town, beavers, foxes, harpies, frogs and bats, their species-specific needs and buildings, affection for a favourite among them and requests for more of them; not the villagers' general mood or the art style.

subjects.label: The Queen and the viceroy
subjects.description: The Queen the player serves and the viceroy role players speak in, her impatience and the effort of pleasing her; not the villagers or the story at large.

subjects.label: Settlement cycle and meta-progression
subjects.description: Each settlement being temporary, won and left behind, the world map resetting after a cycle, the upgrades that carry over, and whether that loop rewards speed over building a perfect town; not the roguelike label itself or how many hours the game lasts.

subjects.label: Storms and the seasons
subjects.description: The storm cycle as a mechanic: rain and thunder that sap the villagers' spirits, surviving the storm season and keeping the fire burning through it; not the general mood or atmosphere it creates.

subjects.label: Villager needs and resolve
subjects.description: Keeping villagers fed, warm and content so they neither starve nor leave: food and fuel running out, satisfaction collapsing, the impossibility of pleasing everyone and cannibalism when the food is gone; not the species themselves or the weather that causes it.

subjects.label: Glades and forest clearing
subjects.description: Cutting into the forest to open glades, the events, crates, graves and resources found there, and the danger of opening more than the settlement can handle; not the map as scenery.

subjects.label: Blueprints and production chains
subjects.description: The settlement's economy: which building makes what, the random blueprint picks that decide it, resource chains, hauling and worker assignment; not building placement as looks or the difficulty verdict.
